## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\) is generated by either specified Schur interval; each family has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [source-backed] The indexed-family graded Nakayama criterion identifies minimal homogeneous generating families with minimal spanning families of \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\), in the integral symmetric-function setting. [source-2, lines 1522-1540]
- [proved] **Conditional \(a=1,b=2\) minimality.** Under the accepted integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation and accepted globalization \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\), both Theorem 5.4 families are minimal.

## Strategy
For \(a=1,b=2\), the source families are
\[
F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2)
=\bigl(s_{i^j},\,s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\,s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})}\bigr)
\]
and
\[
F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2)
=\bigl(s_{i^j},\,s_{(i^j,1)},\,s_{(i^j,2)}\bigr).
\]
They each have \(\binom31=3\) elements and generate \(J_v\) by the cited theorem.

By the accepted quotient result,
\[
Q=J_v/A_+J_v\cong
\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
The accepted degreewise relations give
\[
\bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\qquad \bar y_2=\bar x_2.
\]
Hence the image of \(F_2\) is obtained from the basis given by the image of \(F_1\) through
\[
\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\in\operatorname{GL}_3(\mathbb Z).
\]
Thus the images of both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) are \(\mathbb Z\)-bases of \(Q\). Applying the accepted indexed-family Nakayama criterion to each source-backed generating family shows that neither admits a proper generating subfamily. Therefore both are minimal.

## Gaps
The conclusion is conditional on the accepted integral presentation, the accepted all-degree identification \(J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^3\), and the identification of the relevant positive-degree ideal with that used in the Nakayama application. No unconditional general minimality claim is made.

## Next
The requested conditional \(a=1,b=2\) minimality target is established.
